output.brief: The rejects come from an interaction between two things. Arnholt resin arrives wetter than Quillan, and dryer D5 on Press 5 is degraded. Neither is a problem alone. Arnholt on Press 5 has about 10% rejects, in both shifts and for new and experienced operators alike. Arnholt on Press 7 (good dryer) is 0.8%. Quillan on Press 5 is 0.9%. Arnholt lot A-2291 dried in a good portable dryer and run on Press 5 gave 0.8% rejects. The same lot through D5 gave 10.4%. The second-shift gap exists because all second-shift VX runs on Press 5. The new operators are not the cause. Do not put them on improvement plans. The trial passed because it ran only on Press 7, and the certificates of analysis don't show the moisture actually measured. Do this week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant), restore the −40 alarm limit, and keep Arnholt off D5 until its dew point is verified. Add a feed-throat moisture check for every resin lot. Ask Arnholt about their moisture. Arnholt was only measured from the unconditioned north annex, so whether storage adds moisture is unproven. Don't pay for warehouse space until that is tested. I'm fairly confident in the main finding.
